newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey may set 1997 growth target at four pct.
newsitem.headline: Turkey may set 1997 growth target at four pct.

text.p: Turkey is expected to set its target for 1997 gross national product (GNP) growth rate at four percent, lower than an expected growth of around eight percent this year, economy officials said on Wednesday.
They said year-on-year wholesale price inflation target was likely to be set at 65 percent under the 1997 consolidated bugdet draft which will be finalised by October 17.
Economists expect wholesale inflation to stand at more than 80 percent at the end of this year.

Officials say the budget expenditures may reach 6,700 trillion lira next year. They did not give a figure for the 1997 budget deficit. According to finance ministry offcials, this year's budget deficit will probably hit 1,300 trillion lira.
"The aggregates of the budget are still under study," said an official.
Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said the government was in search of a budget which would provide a real growth in investments and stability in the economy.
Officials say they are seeking to draft a budget which will be able to win backing from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
An IMF team is expected to visit Turkey to examine the Turkish economy and 1997 targets ahead of possible talks for a new stand-by arrangement later this year.
"The IMF and the World Bank will visit Turkey in coming days. The thing to be searched is stability," Ciller told her party's parliamentary group meeting.
A team from the World Bank will arrive in Ankara in mid-November to check Turkey's efforts for structural reforms including privatisation.

The IMF, World Bank and international rating agencies have long been urging Turkey to take structural adjustment measures to lower inflation and narrow the huge public deficit, expected to exceed 10 percent of the country's GNP this year.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said earlier Turkey aimed for a zero-deficit budget in 1997. However, officials say ongoing studies indicated that it would not be achieved.
Over the past decade, Turkey has failed to achieve its key annual economic and budgetary target. The government had aimed to keep 1996 growth rate at 4.5 percent and inflation at 65 percent.
